items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: I heard Red Happy and Henry Zeno and all, Mac Morris and all those guys.

ctx.x: How did, and what did he play Paul Shalini?

Well I don't know what he played. I know the clarinet was, one of his instruments, but he taught all the instruments. He taught everything. Because that's when I, before he started taking a clarinet, I went to him, you know. And he was going to teach me. But I decided I want the low end drums. I heard Red Happy and Henry Zeno and all, Mac Morris and all those guys. And I said, well, I'll switch the drums. So there you are. But clarinet, I really don't want a clarinet. I was cut out for clarinet. I don't know why.…
How did you get the name of T-Boy too?

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: The last time Red Happy was living, his mama was living, he was living, I think it was Sour Tobey Street if I am mistaken.

ctx.x: I was wondering where Red Happy lived, that's another thing.
The last time Red Happy was living, his mama was living, he was living, I think it was Sour Tobey Street if I am mistaken.
He got killed in Cleveland, I understand.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Old drummers, that is the first drummers that inspired you. People like Red Happy you were talking about. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, Red Happy. Just how they played? They had a lot of good drummers.

ctx.x: Big Ike? Yeah, Big Ike, yeah. That's him? Yeah. Just like Chris Kelly. They said Chris Kelly had a lot of glow. All of his glow. All of his glow. Always smart. He's always smart. Did he wear expensive clothes? Well, he's a pretty neat guy. Don't make me terrible.
Old drummers, that is the first drummers that inspired you. People like Red Happy you were talking about.

Yeah, Red Happy. Just how they played? They had a lot of good drummers. Mike Murray was very sensational. Very good drummer. They had a tune that the band used to play. And they had a break. They used to make, you know, Mike Murray always carried a lot of contraptions with them, whistles and different kind of ratchets and all that for breaks, you know. And in this particular tune, he had a chain, you know, like they have on the wagons, a horse and wagon, a chain, a horse to the shaft. Well, they take this chain…
